q: how do animals navigate during migration
a: Animals migrate using a remarkable combination of natural navigation methods. Birds use the sun's position during the day and the stars at night as celestial cues, along with an internal magnetic compass that detects the Earth's magnetic field through specialized proteins called cryptochromes in their eyes. Sea turtles imprint on the magnetic field of their birthplace and return to it years later. Salmon use their sense of smell to detect the unique chemical signature of their home stream. Monarch butterflies use a combination of a sun compass and circadian clock to navigate thousands of miles to specific overwintering sites they've never visited before. Many species also use landmarks, polarized light patterns, and even infrasound (low-frequency sound waves from ocean waves and wind patterns) to orient themselves. The ability to navigate across vast distances without getting lost is one of nature's most impressive feats, involving a complex interplay of genetic programming and learned environmental cues.
